subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: Should iMessage ingest drop non-group, not-from-me DMs before access control when sender canonically matches destination_caller_id and no canonical peer can be recovered?
rationale: That choice controls whether ambiguous local-sender DMs are treated as a peer, dropped, or passed through to authorization and delivery; it is a security/message-delivery boundary that automation should not choose from source alone.

options.title: Repair Only With Canonical Peer Proof
options.body: Use normalizeIMessageHandle for sender, destination, and peer candidates, and only rewrite sender when a different canonical peer is proven by the payload or history.

options.title: Add A Fail-Closed Guard
options.body: Drop unresolved local-sender direct payloads before access control, accepting that malformed legitimate DMs may be skipped until the bridge payload is fixed.

options.title: Pause This Branch
options.body: If the author’s remaining failure is a different root cause, keep this PR draft and track a narrower iMessage issue or replacement fix.

recommendation.title: Repair Only With Canonical Peer Proof
recommendation.body: Use normalizeIMessageHandle for sender, destination, and peer candidates, and only rewrite sender when a different canonical peer is proven by the payload or history.
